question:
The glass gauge on a cylindrical coffee maker shows there are \(45\) cups left when the coffee maker is \(36\%\) full. How many cups of coffee does it hold when it is full?

[Figure 1](figures/1988_AMC_8_Q20_question_fig1.svg)
solution:
The \(45\) cups represent \(36\%\) of the full capacity. Since \(36\%\) consists of 36 equal one-percent portions, divide by 36 to find the amount corresponding to \(1\%\):
\[
45\div 36=1.25\text{ cups}.
\]
A full coffee maker represents \(100\%\), so it holds
\[
1.25\times 100=125\text{ cups}.
\]
The answer is \(125\) cups, choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
